organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror; ilga.gov returned HTTP 503 on access date)
title: Illinois Loan Brokers Act of 1995, 815 ILCS 175/15-5.15 (definition of loan broker)
claim: Defines 'loan broker' as a person who, for a fee, promises to procure or assist in procuring a loan from a third party; excludes banks/credit unions, HUD/VA/agency-approved lenders, insurance producers, sellers financing own product, RMLA licensees, and IDFPR-regulated entities.
excerpt: Loan broker: one who 'promises to procure a loan for any person or assist any person in procuring a loan from any third party' for a fee.
limitations: Mirror may lag the official ILCS text; official ilga.gov unavailable (503) on 2026-11-28. Verify against ilga.gov before reliance.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Illinois Loan Brokers Act of 1995, 815 ILCS 175/15-80 (exemptions)
claim: Exempts from registration: attorneys, CPAs (incidental), real estate licensees in licensed transactions, registered securities persons, creditors, IDFPR-regulated persons, and any person whose fee is wholly contingent on successful procurement of a loan (no fee before a binding commitment other than bona fide third-party fees). No business-loan or dollar-amount exemption. Burden of proof on the person claiming exemption.
excerpt: Exempt if fee is 'wholly contingent on the successful procurement of a loan from a third party'; burden of proof on party claiming exemption.
limitations: Mirror text; check for later amendments. Interpretation that success-fee-only commercial brokers are exempt is our reading, not an agency opinion.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Illinois Loan Brokers Act of 1995, 815 ILCS 175/15-15 (registration)
claim: Non-exempt loan brokers must register with the Illinois Secretary of State (disclosure document, consent to service, bond proof, fee per 15-25); a $25,000 bond is required for brokers handling Truth-in-Lending (consumer) loans; registration renews annually (Jan 1).
excerpt: Bond of $25,000 required for a loan broker handling loans subject to the Truth-in-Lending Act.
limitations: Filing fee amount (Sec. 15-25) not retrieved; MISSING.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Residential Mortgage License Act of 1987, 205 ILCS 635/1-3 (license required)
claim: A license from IDFPR is required to engage in brokering, funding, originating, servicing or purchasing residential mortgage loans; entities engaged solely in commercial mortgage lending are not subject to the licensing requirement; individual MLOs need Article VII licenses.
excerpt: License required for 'brokering, funding, originating, servicing or purchasing' residential mortgage loans; commercial-only lenders not subject.
limitations: Mirror text.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Residential Mortgage License Act of 1987, 205 ILCS 635/1-4 (definitions)
claim: 'Residential mortgage loan' means a loan primarily for personal, family, or household use secured by a mortgage on a dwelling (1-4 units); brokering includes compensation paid by borrower or lender; servicing defined broadly. Business-purpose loans on 1-4 unit investment property appear outside the definition (our reading).
excerpt: Residential mortgage loan: 'any loan primarily for personal, family, or household use that is secured by a mortgage'.
limitations: 'Primarily' not defined; IDFPR interpretive guidance on business-purpose 1-4 unit loans not located (MISSING). Legal reading is analyst interpretation.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Residential Mortgage License Act, 205 ILCS 635/3-5 (net worth)
claim: New RMLA licensees must maintain net worth of $150,000; broker-only licensees $50,000; evidenced by CPA-prepared balance sheet.
excerpt: Broker-only net worth requirement '$50,000' for new licensees; general licensees $150,000.
limitations: Mirror text; may not show later rules by the Secretary.

organization: Illinois Administrative Code via Cornell LII
title: 38 Ill. Adm. Code 1050.490 Bonding Requirements
claim: RMLA licensees must keep an NMLS electronic surety bond: $25,000 for $0-5M prior-year Illinois volume, scaling to $150,000 above $100M.
excerpt: 'each licensee shall file and maintain an electronic surety bond in the NMLS'; $25,000 for $0-$5,000,000 volume.
limitations: Bond premium cost (typically a % of bond, credit-dependent) not sourced.

organization: Illinois General Assembly (statute text via FindLaw mirror)
title: Residential Mortgage License Act, 205 ILCS 635/3-1 (bonds)
claim: Persons handling money for a licensee require a $100,000 fidelity bond; all licensees also maintain a surety bond set by rule.
excerpt: 'fidelity bond in the amount of $100,000'
limitations: Applicability to broker-only licensees not confirmed.

organization: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
title: Mortgage Loan Originators (Bureau of Residential Finance)
claim: All individuals meeting the MLO definition, including owners of entities, must be licensed and must be employed by an Illinois residential mortgage licensee (one at a time).
excerpt: 'Individuals must be employed by an Illinois residential mortgage licensee.'
limitations: Fee amounts and education specifics hosted on NMLS (blocked from this session).

organization: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
title: Bureau of Residential Finance overview
claim: Private mortgages originated in Cook, Kane, Will and Peoria counties must attach a Private Lending Exemption Certificate for recording (anti-predatory lending database program).
excerpt: Private Lending Exemption Certificates must be attached to private mortgages in Cook, Kane, Will, and Peoria counties.
limitations: Did not read the certificate instructions PDF.

title: 12 CFR 1008.105 Minimum loan originator license requirements (SAFE Act, Regulation H)
claim: MLO license requires 20 hours NMLS-approved pre-licensing education, 75% on NMLS test (retest waits), FBI fingerprints, credit report, no felony in prior 7 years (or ever, for fraud/dishonesty), financial responsibility.
excerpt: 'Completed at least 20 hours of pre-licensing education'; test score 'not less than 75 percent'.
limitations: State-specific add-ons for Illinois not retrieved (NMLS site blocked).

title: 13 CFR Part 103 Standards for conducting business with SBA
claim: Defines Agent, Packager, Referral Agent, Lender Service Provider; SBA may suspend/revoke agent privileges; prohibits two-master compensation except packager paid by applicant + referral fee paid by lender with disclosure; LSPs need written agreement reviewed by SBA; LSP fees cannot be charged to the borrower.
excerpt: Referral Agent 'identifies and refers an Applicant to a lender or a lender to an Applicant.'
limitations: Regulation only; enforcement frequency not quantified.

title: SOP 50 10 8.1 Lender and Development Company Loan Programs (Technical Policy Updates)
claim: Agent fees charged to 7(a) applicants on a percentage basis capped at 3% (loans <= $50k), 2% up to $1M plus 0.25% above, $30,000 aggregate max; no flat standard fees and no contingency fees may be charged to applicants; fees > $2,500 require documentation and SBA Form 159; lender may charge up to $2,500 packaging fee without documentation; lender-paid referral fees disclosed on Form 159.
excerpt: Percentage fees may not exceed '3 percent on loans of $50,000 or less'; aggregate maximum '$30,000'.
limitations: Downloaded docx from legacy.sba.gov; lender-paid referral fee levels are not capped by SOP and not published.

title: Texas H.B. 700 (89R, enrolled) - Commercial sales-based financing (Finance Code ch. 398)
claim: Requires commercial sales-based financing providers and brokers to register with the Texas OCCC (existing businesses by 2026-12-31); disclosures for offers under $1M; bans automatic ACH debits unless provider holds first-priority perfected security interest in the deposit account; civil penalties.
excerpt: 'A person may not engage in business as a provider or a commercial sales-based financing broker' without registering with OCCC.
limitations: Implementing OCCC rules not reviewed.

organization: New York State Senate (NY Financial Services Law Art. 8)
title: NY FSL 801 Definitions - commercial finance disclosure
claim: Provider includes a person who solicits and presents specific offers of commercial financing on behalf of a third party (i.e., brokers carry disclosure duties); covers sales-based financing and factoring.
excerpt: Provider includes a person 'who solicits and presents specific offers of commercial financing on behalf of a third party'.
limitations: Paraphrased via fetch tool.

title: NY FSL 802 Exemptions - commercial finance disclosure
claim: Exempts financial institutions, transactions over $2.5M, real-property-secured transactions, true leases, and providers with <=5 NY transactions per 12 months.
excerpt: Exempt: 'an individual commercial financing transaction in an amount over two million five hundred thousand dollars.'
limitations: Disclosure content (Sec. 803) not reviewed.

title: California Financial Code 22004 (broker definition, California Financing Law)
claim: A 'broker' under the CFL is anyone engaged in negotiating or performing any act as broker in connection with loans made by a finance lender; brokering commercial loans to California borrowers generally requires a CFL license.
excerpt: Broker: 'engaged in the business of negotiating or performing any act as broker in connection with loans made by a finance lender.'
limitations: Official leginfo and DFPI sites returned 403; licensing cost not retrieved.

title: California Financial Code 22602 (unlicensed referral compensation)
claim: CFL lenders may pay unlicensed persons only for bare referrals on commercial loans <=36% APR with lender underwriting/reporting; unlicensed referrers may not negotiate, advise, collect documents, etc., unless <=5 loans in 12 months.
excerpt: Referrers may not take part in negotiations, prepare documents or collect loan documents (paraphrase).
limitations: Mirror text.

title: Illinois Interest Act, 815 ILCS 205/4
claim: General written-contract cap 9%, but any rate may be charged on business loans to business entities/sole proprietors operating a business, loans to corporations, and loans secured by real estate mortgages (subject to PLPA and residential prepayment restrictions).
excerpt: Any rate on 'any business loan to a business association or copartnership'.
limitations: Mirror text; interaction with other Acts not analyzed in depth.

title: Illinois Predatory Loan Prevention Act, 815 ILCS 123/15-5-5 (rate cap)
claim: Lenders may not contract for or receive charges exceeding 36% APR (military APR method) on covered consumer loans.
excerpt: 'a lender shall not contract for or receive charges exceeding a 36% annual percentage rate'
limitations: Scope/coverage sections and anti-evasion provisions not retrieved here.

title: County Business Patterns 2023 (US and state files, NAICS 5223xx)
claim: NAICS 522310 (mortgage and nonmortgage loan brokers): US 9,792 establishments, 54,952 employees, $4.91B payroll; Illinois 279 establishments (233 with <5 employees), 1,120 employees, $93.6M payroll.
excerpt: Illinois NAICS 522310: 279 establishments, 1,120 employees, $93,583k annual payroll (2023).
limitations: Excludes nonemployer sole proprietors (many brokers); establishments not firms; file downloaded by another Atlas agent from Census.

title: Statistics of U.S. Businesses 2022 (US & state, 6-digit NAICS, with receipts)
claim: NAICS 522310 US: 9,631 firms, receipts $18.3B; 7,600 firms with <5 employees had receipts $2.79B (~$367k/firm) and payroll $760M (~$100k/firm). Illinois: 210 firms <5 employees, receipts $68.6M (~$326k/firm), payroll $23.5M. 5-9 employee firms US avg receipts ~$1.25M.
excerpt: US 522310 <5-employee firms: 7,600 firms, receipts $2,790,326k (2022).
limitations: 2022 receipts (rate-shock year; mortgage volumes depressed vs 2020-21). Excludes nonemployers. Mixes mortgage and nonmortgage brokers. Per-firm averages are analyst calculations.

title: 12 CFR 1026.43(e)(3) QM points and fees limits
claim: Qualified mortgages limit total points and fees (including broker compensation) to 3% of loan amount for loans >= $100,000 (indexed), with dollar caps for smaller loans.
excerpt: Points and fees may not exceed '3 percent of the total loan amount' for loans >= $100,000 (indexed).
limitations: Indexed 2026 thresholds not retrieved.

title: 12 CFR 1026.36(d) Loan originator compensation rule
claim: In consumer dwelling-secured credit, loan originator compensation may not be based on loan terms or proxies (no yield-spread upselling); constrains broker pricing flexibility.
excerpt: No loan originator shall receive compensation 'based on a term of a transaction'.
limitations: Applies to consumer-purpose loans only.

title: UWM Holdings 10-K for fiscal year 2025
claim: UWM (largest wholesale lender) originated $163.4B in 2025, average loan $388k; states roughly 2 of every 10 US mortgages originate through the wholesale (broker) channel; discloses Escue class action and Ohio AG suit alleging brokers were captive/steered borrowers.
excerpt: 'approximately 2 of every 10 loans are originated through the wholesale channel.'
limitations: Incumbent lender economics, not broker economics; litigation allegations unproven.

title: Partner programs (Broker Services, Equipment Vendor, Affiliate)
claim: Large nonbank small-business lender (deals $10k-$500k) does not publish commission rates and states its broker program is at full capacity for ISOs and brokers; working capital repaid daily/weekly over 4-24 months.
excerpt: 'We are currently at full capacity for all ISOs and Brokers.'
limitations: Marketing page; no compensation figures.

title: Broker partner page
claim: Business-purpose residential investor lender (fix & flip, rental, construction, bridge) reports 1,000+ broker partners nationwide; broker pricing available only via AE/portal (not published).
excerpt: '1,000+' brokers nationwide partner with Lima One.
limitations: Self-reported marketing claim; no compensation data.

title: Lendio franchise page (HTTP 404 on access date)
claim: Lendio's former loan-brokerage franchise page returns 404 on 2026-11-28, suggesting the franchise offering is no longer marketed (not confirmed).
excerpt: HTTP 404 Not Found for lendio.com/franchise on 2026-11-28.
limitations: A 404 is not proof of discontinuation; FDD not reviewed.

title: Partner with Us: Earn Commissions on Funded Loans (FAQ)
claim: Published referral commission: standard 2% of funded loan amount, paid ~10-15 days after funding, plus SBA volume-tier incentives; products SBA 7(a) $50k-$350k, bank term loans $50k-$300k, LOC $50k-$100k; no minimum referral volume; partners undergo background checks.
excerpt: 'The standard referral commission is 2% of the funded loan amount, typically paid 10–15 days after funding'
limitations: Published schedule, not evidence of realized partner earnings; approval/fund rates of referrals not disclosed.

title: Broker Loan Program
claim: Business-purpose investor lender publishes broker compensation of YSP up to 2.50% on fix-and-flip/bridge and DSCR rental loans; loans $75k-$5M; Platinum tier requires $6M+ bridge volume in 6 months and <=2% DQ on seasoned loans.
excerpt: 'Earn YSP up to 2.50% on fix-and-flip/ bridge and DSCR rental loan options.'
limitations: Maximum, not typical realized comp; broker licensing requirements by state not stated on page.

organization: Federal Reserve Banks (Small Business Credit Survey)
title: 2026 Report on Employer Firms: Findings from the 2025 SBCS
claim: 38% of employer firms applied for a loan, line of credit or MCA in prior 12 months; of applicants 42% received full amount, 36% partial, 22% none; small banks 57% full approval; 60% of online-lender borrowers said costs were higher than expected (vs 37% small banks).
excerpt: 42% received the full amount sought, 36% some, 22% none (paraphrase of page).
limitations: Convenience sample (6,525 firms); broker usage not reported; lender-type approval rates only partially reported on summary page.

title: Manhattan Bridge Capital 10-K for FY2025
claim: Small public hard-money lender with six employees: FY2025 revenue $8.67M (interest $7.18M + origination fees $1.49M), net income $5.11M, equity $43.1M (net income/equity ~11.9%), loans originated $35.3M; rates typically 9-12.5% plus 0-2 points; loan sizes $40k-$3.6M; LTV usually <=75% for acquisitions; credit lines $42.5M.
excerpt: 'As of December 31, 2025, we employed six employees.'
limitations: Incumbent economics (18+ years, bank lines, NY metro); ROE is after leverage; not a new-entrant benchmark.

title: Triumph Financial 10-K for FY2025 (Factoring segment)
claim: Factoring segment purchased $11.7B of receivables (6.68M invoices, avg $1,752; transportation avg $1,717); revenue $158.3M; yield on average net funds employed 14.87%; operating margin 30.7%; describes fraud as the most material risk of loss in factoring.
excerpt: Risk model 'largely geared toward early detection and mitigation of fraud, which we believe represents the most material risk of loss'
limitations: Bank-funded scale incumbent; new-entrant cost of funds and loss rates far worse.

title: Carrier payment solutions / Select Carrier Program
claim: Large trucking factor advertises same-day invoice factoring and a Select Carrier Program locking a rate of 2.5% or less on all invoices.
excerpt: 'lock in a rate of 2.5% or less on all invoices'
limitations: Program-specific marketing rate; qualification terms not shown.

title: Walker & Dunlop 10-K for FY2025 (Capital Markets segment)
claim: Origination fee rate 83 bps of total debt financing volume in 2025 (92 bps in 2024); brokered loans were 54% of debt financing volume; Capital Markets personnel expense $475M vs revenue $647M.
excerpt: Origination Fee Rate 83 basis points (2025) vs 92 (2024).
limitations: Large-balance institutional CRE incumbent; small-balance broker fees differ (typically higher % on smaller loans; not verified).

title: ELFA Research hub
claim: Describes a $1.5 trillion U.S. equipment finance industry; CAPEX Finance Index headline says new deal activity could top $140 billion by year-end 2026.
excerpt: 'the $1.5 trillion U.S. equipment finance industry'
limitations: Association headline figures; broker share of volume not given; underlying reports member-gated.

title: About NEFA
claim: NEFA members include independent and bank-owned lessors, funding sources and commercial finance brokers, i.e., an established broker-to-funder network exists in equipment finance.
excerpt: Members include 'independent and bank-owned lessors and funding sources, commercial finance brokers'
limitations: No compensation or volume data.

title: Property Assessed Clean Energy Act, 50 ILCS 50/5 (definitions)
claim: Illinois C-PACE covers privately owned commercial, industrial, non-residential agricultural, multifamily (5+ units) and nonprofit property (not single-family); capital providers buy PACE bonds; program administrators run programs for governmental units.
excerpt: Program administrator acts 'on behalf of or at the discretion of the governmental unit'.
limitations: Fee/compensation rules and list of active Illinois PACE programs not retrieved.

title: Active FDIC-insured institutions headquartered in Illinois (index 2026-11-27)
claim: 321 active FDIC-insured institutions headquartered in Illinois, 267 with total assets <= $1B; 4,204 active nationally.
excerpt: meta.total = 321 (STALP:IL AND ACTIVE:1); 267 with ASSET <= $1,000,000 thousand.
limitations: Excludes credit unions (NCUA) and nonbank lenders; counts institutions not loan-review budgets.

title: FIL-55-2020 Interagency Guidance on Credit Risk Review Systems
claim: Regulators expect a system of independent, ongoing credit risk review with qualified, independent reviewers; applies to all FDIC-supervised institutions including those under $1B - creating recurring demand for (often outsourced) loan review.
excerpt: 'a system of independent, ongoing credit risk review and appropriate communication to management and the board'
limitations: Guidance does not mandate outsourcing; market prices for outsourced loan review not sourced.

title: Partnership Opportunities (broker and referral partners)
claim: Working-capital/MCA funder runs broker ('funding partners') and referral partner programs, self-reports $5B+ financed and 50,000+ small businesses; commission levels not published.
excerpt: 'Industry-leading commissions' (no figures published).
limitations: Marketing claims; no compensation or clawback terms.

title: Partners (factoring/ABL broker referrals)
claim: Factoring/ABL provider states brokers earn commissions on referred deals, paid upon funding, with incentives for repeat/high-volume partners; rates not published.
excerpt: 'Commissions are paid promptly upon funding, and additional incentives may be available'
limitations: No published rate or trailing-commission duration.

title: Rollovers as Business Start-Ups (ROBS) Compliance Project
claim: IRS says ROBS are not abusive tax avoidance transactions but are 'questionable'; promoters aggressively market them; noncompliant plans can be disqualified.
excerpt: ROBS plans 'are questionable because they may solely benefit one individual'
limitations: Page undated; promoter fee levels not sourced.

title: 17 CFR 275.203(m)-1 Private fund adviser exemption
claim: U.S. advisers solely to qualifying private funds with < $150M private fund assets are exempt from SEC registration (exempt reporting adviser); state-level (Illinois) adviser rules apply separately.
excerpt: Exempt if it 'Manages private fund assets of less than $150 million.'
limitations: Illinois Securities Department adviser registration/exemption requirements not retrieved (MISSING).
